Posted May 9, 2003
(MarijuanaNews note: For sometime I have been writing about the prohibitionist counterattack in Canada.
The Prohibitionist Counterattack In Canada Runs Into Some Flack. RCMP Challenged. And I Have Fun Writing A Letter to the Editor.
and
 The Agenda for the Prohibitionist Counterattack in Canada. Analysis by Richard Cowan
and
 The Prohibitionist Counterattack in Canada -- DEA Is Their Middle Name. May Conference In Vancouver Requires Serious Response.

It seems to be coming in the guise of the proposed decriminalization bill that will be introduced in Ottawa in the near future.
See
 Canadian Prime Minister Commits To Decriminalization Soon Just 23 Years After He First Said He Was In Favor. It Was A Good Idea Then, But John Conroy Thinks It May Be Dangerous Now.

Moreover, it is increasingly obvious that shipping magnate Paul Martin, the man virtually certain to be the next Prime Minister, is a hardline prohibitionist. He even talks about winning the war on drugs. Canadians like to joke about Americans ignorance about Canada, but Canadian ignorance about DEAland is no joke. In this case it is a tragedy.

Martin is not scheduled to replace Jean Chretien until the PM retires next February, so Martin has limited influence on legislation until then.

As I pointed out earlier this week, the fact that the Supreme Court is reviewing the constitutionality of all the cannabis laws inhibits the prohibitionists, because if the hardliners did what they would really like to do, that would increase the likelihood of the Court overturning the laws.
See
 Canadian Supreme Court Hearings Could Make History, But They Are Only Good For A Joke In DEAland Media. Filed Under Oddly Enough. Dude, Is This Journalism?

There are also major differences between the Canadian and DEAland legal systems. Canada follows the European model of having much shorter sentences for all crimes than DEAland. Moreover, prosecutors here are not elected politicians who are trying to score political points by grandstanding with harsh sentences.

Here in British Columbia, the conservative (Liberal party) provincial government has closed jails and court houses to save money, even as the dimwitted Provincial Solicitor General was calling for a crackdown on growers. Also BC judges tend to oppose longer sentences, although there are a few exceptions.

Nonetheless, it is clear that we should demand an international debate on cannabis prohibition, including DEAland precisely because the Bush regime is intent on interfering in the internal affairs of Canada and everywhere else, for that matter.

Actually, if Canada were to propose such a debate on an international scale, it would probably frighten the DEAland government so much that they would just shut up. It is hard enough to get anyone official to debate NORML even on a radio talk show.

However, whether or not DEAland wants to debate, Canada needs to have one for its own benefit. If the Supreme Court strikes down all of the laws, the country needs to understand how it can regulate cannabis. If the Court leaves all or part of cannabis prohibition in place, then the country needs to know what to do next, because the problems of prohibition are not going away, and neither are the demands for freedom for the cannabis community.

Decriminalization is a half-step at best, and as the article below makes clear, it could very well be a step in the wrong direction.

We are winning in Canada and the prohibitionist know it and will do anything they can to stop it. An open debate is our best battleground.)

Excerpted from
Crack down on traffickers, Martin urges
'The war on drugs is critically important,' Liberal front-runner says
By Peter O'Neil
From The Ottawa Citizen
http://www.canada.com/ottawa/ottawacitizen/
CanWest News Service
May 9, 2003

Canada must take dramatic measures to win the " war " against illegal drugs, Liberal leadership front-runner Paul Martin said yesterday.
(Marijuana news note: Yes, just as has been sooo successful everywhere else??)

Mr. Martin, while supportive of the federal plan to decriminalize marijuana possession and permit safe injection sites for drug addicts, called for a crackdown on the organized criminal groups running the marijuana cultivation industry based in Ontario, Quebec and especially British Columbia.

" The war against drugs is critically important, " Mr. Martin said yesterday.

" I think whether we would decriminalize or not, we should deal with these issues. By the way, this is not just a Vancouver issue. This is an issue right across the country. This is a massive issue in Quebec. "

The Chrétien government, which announced plans for a National Drug Strategy in the 2002 throne speech, has always refused to adopt the U.S.-style " war on drugs " rhetoric that focuses on law enforcement.

" I don't know if we use the term, either, but I mean certainly, yes, a massive effort (is needed), " Mr. Martin said.

" I think the penalties ought to be very severe and I think the government ought to crack down as much as possible. I think the government ought to crack down, period. "

An RCMP intelligence report has warned that Canada, thanks to weak sentencing laws, has become a " haven " for indoor marijuana grow operations that are run by outlaw biker gangs and Vietnamese gangs prone to " extreme violence. "
See
 http://www.rcmp-grc.gc.ca/crimint/cultivation_e.htm
(MarijuanaNews note: DEAland produces far more cannabis than Canada. If they increase the penalties, there will be more organized crime, not less.)
See
 Organized Crime In The Marijuana Trade.
Why More " Law Enforcement " is Counterproductive.
An Excellent Halifax Editorial Says, " Marijuana laws encourage crime. "

U.S. Ambassador Paul Cellucci said recently that Canada, if it wants to avoid border troubles, needs to send a signal that it will move against growers and traffickers if it goes ahead with decriminalization of possession of small amounts of marijuana.
See
 DEAland Threats Make The News In Canada, Headlines In Vancouver, But Disrupting Canadian Trade Would Hurt American Companies, So It Is Important That the Threats Not Be Publicized At Home.

The Canadian Police Association said this week the government shouldn't rush to decriminalize marijuana possession without taking stronger measures on the law enforcement side.
(MarijuanaNews note: The head of the Canadian Police Association actually told the Washington Post that Canada has replaced Mexico as the leading source of cannabis. He also lied to the Canadian Senate about the Dutch experience.)
See
 Canadian Police Association Demonstrates The Role of Ideology in the Maintenance of Marijuana Prohibition. Sweden Ideal While the Dutch Are the Worst. Analysis by Richard Cowan.
and
 The Prohibitionist Police State Versus The People. Analysis By Richard Cowan
and
 As Canada Moves Toward Some Form Of Decriminalization, Canadian Narks and Walters Escalate Lying. The New Math. Canada Replaces Mexico As Leading Supplier of Cannabis. And If You Believe That

While Solicitor General Wayne Easter said yesterday he favours a more punitive system, the 2002 throne speech didn't emphasize a tougher law-and-order approach.

" The government will also implement a national drug strategy to address addiction while promoting public safety, " the speech promised.

" It will expand the number of drug treatment courts. It will act on the results of parliamentary consultations with Canadians on options for change in our drug laws, including the possibility of the decriminalization of marijuana possession. "

Mr. Martin said the government plan to decriminalize possession of 30 grams or less of cannabis could help discourage drug use.

" I've talked to a lot of police who actually say that, 'Listen, for very small amounts we would often let the people go because we're not going to (charge them with) criminal offences. We actually think it would be a greater deterrence if you have a fine.' "
